uslaw-usc-t1-s7:
Section 7 of Title 1 of the United States Code defines marriage for the whole of federal law. It stands in the chapter of Title 1 that gives rules of construction for statutes. Whenever marital status matters under a federal law, rule, or regulation, this section supplies the test.

A person counts as married if the marriage joins two individuals and is valid where it was entered into. For a marriage made inside a state, validity in that state is the measure. For a marriage made outside any state, two things must hold. It must be valid in the place where it was made, and it must be one that could have been entered into in a state. The term State is then defined to include the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and other territories.
uslaw-usc-t2-s7:
Section 7 of Title 2 of the United States Code fixes the time of election for Congress. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the chapter on election of senators and representatives. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. One national election day is set for federal offices.

The Tuesday next after the first Monday in November, in every even numbered year, is the day, the text states. On that day each state and territory elects Representatives and Delegates to the Congress that begins the next January. A single shared date, rather than scattered state dates, has shaped American campaigns and turnout for generations of voters.
